text:
Romi Patel: Quick announcement: launching an SDK telemetry opt-in policy draft. Goal: make all non-essential runtime telemetry opt-in by default in client SDKs. We want clearer controls and a visible opt-in badge in docs. Preview: https://docs.redwood/preview/sdk-telemetry-opt-in
Marcus Lee: What falls under "non-essential"?
Romi Patel: Examples: anonymized sample payload hashes for debugging, client-side performance metrics (latency histogram sent from SDK), and usage counters for opt-in features. Auth/authz tokens and full request bodies are explicitly excluded.
Hannah Kim: How will this affect hosted customers using our default hosted SDK builds?
Romi Patel: Hosted customers who use our hosted SDK bundles will have telemetry off by default until GA. We'll provide a one-line opt-in: `RedwoodClient(telemetry_opt_in=True)` and env `RW_SDK_TELEMETRY=1`. We'll also surface a changelog entry and a small banner in the docs with exact fields collected.
LegalBot: Need precise language about retention, aggregation, and PII. Also specify that telemetry helps us prioritize infra and model work. Provide an opt-out SLA clause for enterprise customers.
Marcus Lee: For Dedicated/Private installs, telemetry must remain opt-in and disabled by default. Can we ship a telemetry shim that logs locally and exposes a `redwood.telemetry.flush()` so infra owners can review before sending?
Romi Patel: Yes 100% agreed. We'll ship a local buffer mode `telemetry_mode=\"buffered\"` that writes gzipped records to `$XDG_STATE_HOME/redwood/telemetry/` and provides a CLI `redwood telemetry inspect`. That will be documented in the private deployment guide.
Hannah Kim: Docs tasks? I can add the opt-in snippets and a small FAQ about how we use telemetry. Also include a sample minimal payload schema for auditing.
DocsBot: Draft preview page: https://docs.redwood/preview/telemetry-policy. I've added the badge mockup `telemetry:opt-in` for SDK quickstarts.
Marcus Lee: Rollout plan and timeline?
Romi Patel: Internal preview today -> docs preview 48h -> SDK release draft (4.3.2) with opt-in flags in tests -> GA in 6 weeks pending legal. We'll mark the old implicit telemetry behavior deprecated with a 90-day notice before enforcement.
LegalBot: I'll review the policy and the customer-facing blurb. Please include explicit data categories, retention limits (suggest 90 days aggregated, 30 days raw buffer for buffered mode), and contact for data subject requests.
Hannah Kim: Adding a CHANGELOG fragment and a migration snippet for Solutions: `# to enable opt-in telemetry
client = RedwoodClient(telemetry_opt_in=True)
export RW_SDK_TELEMETRY=1`
Marcus Lee: Support teams need a short runbook for diagnosing when telemetry is off. Can we add `SupportBot` quick commands like `supportbot show-telemetry-config <org>`?
SupportBot: Added runbook draft: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/telemetry. Commands: `redwood-cli telemetry:status --org <org>` and `redwood-cli telemetry:flush --org <org>` (requires auth).
Romi Patel: Great. Final asks: Legal to sign off on retention language, Docs to publish the banner and examples, DevEx to add a CI test ensuring telemetry flags are present in released SDKs. We'll reconvene after legal review.
Hannah Kim: I'll tag the preview PR with `telemetry-preview` and ping @LegalBot.
Marcus Lee: Thanks. Let's be explicit in the changelog so customers scanning releases don't miss a behavioral change.
Romi Patel: Agreed. I'll draft the customer-facing FAQ and a small public blog post for when GA happens. Thanks everyone.
